Complete one implementation change

Use this procedure through sdw-run for one authorized change. Follow the execution procedure for registry selection, dispatch, evidence, coordination and recovery. The selected plan supplies attempt limits; this procedure does not introduce another set of caps.

1. Select and prepare

Confirm the problem, acceptance criteria, project, ticket, change and dependencies. Read current contracts and relevant target instructions. Inspect the registered queue, then claim the selected change and create or resume its owned worktree. Prepare the declared environment. Preserve unrelated work and retain the base revision, authority, scope and ownership in the intake and ledger.

2. Harden the contract

Apply design hardening to new or changed implementation contracts. Reconcile valid existing artifacts instead of rewriting them. Establish observable scenarios, interfaces, failure cases and a test plan. Do not begin dependent implementation while required design acceptance is incomplete. Pure review and setup requests end within their authorized phase.

3. Implement bounded slices

The lead derives a compact scenario-to-task map from the accepted design. Assign each writer exact exclusive source and test files, relevant contracts, dependencies, checks and an output contract. Shared files have one owner at a time. Keep assignments within the registered areas and task scope.

Integrate completed slices and run their relevant checks. Record actual behavior and justified design decisions in the owning artifacts. Do not weaken a requirement to excuse a failed implementation or skip an independent review because a writer reports success.

4. Review and repair

Apply implementation review to the integrated change. Both lenses cover the full affected behavior, including shared interfaces and relevant consumers. Adjudicate a nonempty findings batch and assign coherent repairs. Reserve enough allowance for fresh independent review after every material fix.

Run checks required by project registration and changed behavior. Tests validate implementation; source bundles and ledger checks validate evidence bindings. Neither replaces the other. Broaden successful verification only when new changes, failures or unresolved concerns justify it.

5. Finish artifacts and final acceptance

After implementation and verification, complete the same-change specification lifecycle. Check delivered tasks, sync full requirement bodies, archive completed work and repair references. Capture the resulting final artifacts and renew affected review acceptance, including design evidence changed by archive relocation.

Bind all required checks and both review phases to the relevant final inputs. Inspect the full diff, including deletions, modes, new files and shared metadata. Report incomplete evidence or unresolved findings instead of claiming readiness.

6. Hand off within authority

Prepare a concise change summary linking the ticket and OpenSpec artifacts, with checks, review coverage and limitations. Publish or merge only within the applicable scope of authority and after the runtime gates pass. Preserve the ledger and original evidence for handoff. Cleanup and the next task are separate actions.

Installed development workflow

Open the generated visual handbook in a browser to read the process diagram and current profile tables offline. Markdown and the catalog remain the maintained sources. Rebuild the page from the Git worktree root with:

uv run --locked --project agentic_harness python agentic_harness/tools/build.py
uv run --locked --project agentic_harness python agentic_harness/tools/build.py --check

Start with the policy map. It identifies the required instructions for the current phase. The execution procedure connects project selection, original evidence, isolated workspaces and durable review accounting.

  • Development lifecycle
  • OpenSpec ownership and completion
  • Plan profiles and machine-readable catalog
  • Complete pipeline
  • Design hardening
  • Implementation review
  • Worker role contract

Each adopted OpenSpec home keeps project settings beside its specifications:

  • openspec/config.yaml (or an existing config.yml) selects the native schema and supplies project context, artifact rules and supported operation guidance.
  • openspec/workflow.yaml supplies this workflow's source scopes, executable checks, environment preparation, lockfiles and evidence exclusions. Paths are relative to the Git worktree root; checks also run from that root.

projects.yaml is the internal index of stable project identifiers and OpenSpec directories. Runs record those identifiers. The installer maintains the index; choose a directory when starting work. Legacy installations can still read their inline settings until a reviewed update moves them beside OpenSpec. The installer records its version and managed file hashes in install.json. Application settings and specifications stay project-owned.

Run the entrypoint from the consumer repository's Git worktree root:

uv run --locked --project agentic_harness python \
  agentic_harness/tools/harness.py project

For a component, append --at services/api, replacing that path with the directory containing its openspec/. Without --at, the command uses the nearest adopted OpenSpec home from the current directory, or the sole configured project if no local home is found. Ambiguity or a nearer unadopted home stops selection. Keep the returned id in the run's machine requests and evidence.

The OpenSpec CLI is installed locally with npm --prefix agentic_harness ci --ignore-scripts. Route it through harness.py openspec --at services/api -- COMMAND, or omit --at under the same selection rules. OpenSpec owns its generated files; our skills use sdw-* and retain the execution, independent review and acceptance gates.

Workflow instruction map

Read this map after the target repository's applicable instructions and the selected project registration. Links are references, not automatic imports. Resolve Markdown links relative to their containing file and operational paths from the assigned repository or worktree root. Report a missing required file before starting work that depends on it.

Exactly one config filename is supported; preserve the existing choice. Product facts, build commands and domain constraints belong to that project; this package does not supply them.

Entry points and authority

sdw-run, sdw-harden and sdw-review are package-owned entry points. They select a registered project and require these shared policies. They do not replace OpenSpec-generated skills or grant permission to implement, publish or merge.

Installation adds explicit routing to existing repository instructions. It must preserve unrelated instructions and agent settings. Read the routed documents; do not assume that discovering a skill has loaded every policy or selected the correct OpenSpec root.

The installed version supplies common process rules. Project registration binds scope, specification home, checks and environment preparation. User instructions and applicable host or repository constraints still apply. Resolve a conflict explicitly; never silently replace the target project's rules.

Plan profiles

plans.yaml is the machine-readable source for the three shipped profiles: budget, balanced and smart. balanced is the catalog default. Selecting a profile records a run decision; it does not rewrite user settings or switch an already running lead. Follow the execution policy.

Read the catalog

Each step records its responsibility, count scope, context profile and allowed writes. Each plan binds that step to Codex and Claude model/effort routes and a successful minimum and attempt maximum. A maximum is a ceiling, not a target. Conditional steps with zero minimum run only when needed. A zero maximum requires a recorded extension before launch.

Inspect exact routes and limits with the installed harness interpreter:

python agentic_harness/tools/harness.py plans routes --plan balanced

The catalog preserves the source workflow's model pairs and budgets as explicit profile data. They are supported requested settings only when the target account, client and session can verify them. Equal effort names do not establish equal reasoning, quality, latency or cost across providers. No measured equivalence or savings is claimed.

Counting and acceptance

D and I are shared design and implementation round counters. Each round launches both required independent lenses against the same frozen revision; the second reviewer is not a second round. The clean_rounds value specifies how many complete clean rounds must concern the accepted unchanged inputs.

Count admitted attempts, including failed launches, repairs and retries. Count implementers per predeclared slice and adjudicators per phase. Routine lead coordination consumes usage but is not a hidden worker launch. Applicable stages come from the request; review-only work never starts authors or implementers.

Before a repair, retain enough allowance for the full clean minimum afterward. When that cannot fit, use the extension process before editing. A material final integration edit consumes its repair allowance, invalidates affected acceptance and requires a new frozen capture. Stop once the selected plan's acceptance conditions and required checks pass.

Context and configuration

The catalog's lookup, context, standard and deep profiles set initial packet, working-input, result and handoff targets. Deep context requires scoped authority. Use the smallest verified effective capacity and retain room for tool-result growth and the runtime reserve. A target cannot enlarge a provider's window. Save decisions and unresolved work before a handoff.

Project bindings configure paths, checks and environment preparation. Profile changes are separate package configuration changes and must pass catalog validation. Do not edit generated adapters to create another route table or claim an arbitrary catalog extension is supported by this version.

The runtime records the chosen catalog with each ledger. Existing runs retain their original meaning during an update. Historical source-repository runs are not imported or relabeled by installing this package.

Repository boundaries

This package governs development within explicitly adopted scopes. It does not define the target application's architecture, language, data model or runtime. Read the target repository's instructions and relevant source before proposing behavior or claiming a capability exists.

Scope and ownership

Select the OpenSpec directory that owns the requested work. Its openspec/workflow.yaml lists adopted source areas in code_roots, while openspec/config.yaml (or the existing config.yml) holds native project context and rules. Paths in workflow settings are relative to the Git worktree root. One OpenSpec home may cover several source and test directories. These boundaries are not a filesystem sandbox. Do not infer write permission from a dependency, a shared parent directory or the ability to read a file.

Use the selected id returned by harness.py project in intake, coordination, dispatch and evidence records. The internal projects.yaml index retains that identity across updates. Directory selection happens before a run; a later working-directory change must not rebind an admitted request. Legacy inline settings remain readable until the installer migrates them in a reviewed update.

Each task has a bounded intake scope. Each writer owns exact files within that scope and the registered areas: adopted code roots and the selected project's openspec/ metadata. Shared configuration changes must be named explicitly. Inspect the full diff before acceptance to catch unassigned additions, deletions and renames. Preserve unrelated edits and other contributors' work.

Use a dedicated worktree for implementation. Keep the shared checkout and other worktrees intact. Never reset, stash, clean or remove another task's work as an automatic recovery step. Use normal, non-forced removal only after checking ownership, dirty state, active assignments and retained dependencies.

Project checks and environments

openspec/workflow.yaml supplies required checks as argument arrays, not shell fragments. Checks run from the Git worktree root. Use the project's documented setup and declared lockfiles. Do not assume that every target uses Python, uv, npm, or a particular application test command because the workflow itself uses Python and Node.

Prepare the assigned worktree without changing the project's intended dependency versions. An intentional dependency-lock change requires environment preparation and a recorded rebind before execution continues. Preserve the previous fingerprint and preparation evidence; a new digest alone is not preparation. Changing which lockfiles or preparation commands are declared changes the environment policy itself and requires a newly scoped run, not a byte rebind.

Run checks appropriate to changed behavior and the project's requirements. Fix relevant failures. Do not repeat successful checks on unchanged inputs solely to consume a quota. Framework documentation-rendering checks belong to framework development unless a target explicitly registers them.

Data and external actions

Keep credentials, private exports and operational state out of committed examples and retained review source. Use synthetic fixtures where practical. Declare project-specific evidence exclusions in openspec/workflow.yaml. Do not assume that ordinary directories named data, runtime, inputs or out contain private material in every project. Inspect selected source before capture.

Evidence exclusions are enforced across registered projects so a dependency read respects its owner's privacy policy. Deleted originals also retain the pinned base's exclusions; removing an exclusion does not expose a deleted file.

Preserve live data, manual decisions and external state. Tests and command help do not authorize a live import, deployment, destructive migration or paid model experiment. Follow existing applicable authorization, and obtain missing authorization only for the action that needs it.

Report verified facts, assumptions, incomplete checks and unavailable evidence separately. A passing structural validator does not prove runtime quality, complete review, model equivalence or production readiness.

Development scope and lifecycle

This policy connects one bounded request, its specification, implementation and verification. Follow the OpenSpec policy for specification state and the execution policy for agent runs.

Intake, tickets and authorization

Record the problem, intended outcome, acceptance criteria, project, affected paths, dependencies and applicable authorization before implementation. Select one bounded ticket and keep its description consistent with the owning change. The execution runtime requires a verified ticket observation for code writers; do not invent a ticket or remote observation to satisfy that gate.

The supplied remote adapter targets GitHub. Repository identity comes from the target project and its remote, never from the workflow's source repository. Other trackers need a separately implemented and verified adapter.

Planning, review, implementation, publication, merge and cleanup are distinct actions. Use authority already provided for the scope; do not ask for it again. A planning or setup request does not authorize implementation of product behavior. Installing this package does not authorize posting issues, comments or pull requests. Observe the target project's decision-recording rules.

Worktrees and reviewable changes

Implement in an owned worktree from the agreed base revision. Use the target repository's branch and commit conventions, with a ticket reference. Keep each commit and pull request coherent. Include no unrelated local changes.

One pull request covers one independently reviewable implementation scope. Its description links the ticket and owning OpenSpec change and records relevant checks, review evidence and limitations. Publish only within the granted scope. Merge additionally requires merge authority and verification of the current head; readiness or permission to open a pull request does not imply it.

Change selection and queue

Resolve the registered project's queue from the repository root. Preserve one queue and one specification authority for that project. Queue entries retain stable identifiers and dependencies; their order is explicit in the queue, not in filenames or numeric identifiers.

The current runtime accepts change IDs shaped as YY-MM-DD-NNN-short-description. Keep existing IDs and creation metadata stable. Do not rename or renumber changes to reorder work. Keep archived entries as history and keep queue dependencies consistent with proposals.

An explicitly selected change takes precedence over default selection, while its prerequisites still apply. When implementation is authorized without a named change, inspect the first unfinished eligible queue item. Queue inspection and selection are read-only; ownership requires a separate claim. Report a selected blocked dependency instead of silently substituting another task.

Missing design or tasks, an empty checklist, an archived label or a merged pull request cannot establish delivery. Check actual artifacts, completed work and verification evidence. Handoff of one task does not start the next queue item.

Complete the same change

The implementation pull request also owns its truthful specification lifecycle. After implementation and verification, mark delivered tasks, synchronize the implemented deltas and archive completed work with the pinned OpenSpec CLI. Update affected links, navigation, queue state and project context in that change. Do not create a later cleanup pull request merely to declare already delivered behavior complete.

Keep incomplete or partially delivered changes active. If work is split, record the new ownership and acceptance boundaries without duplicate normative specifications. Historical work and evidence keep their original meaning.

OpenSpec authority and completion

OpenSpec owns product change artifacts and capability specifications. This package adds execution and acceptance rules around its pinned CLI. Read the selected project's context and instructions before using a generated skill.

Select one authority

Choose the directory containing the intended openspec/. From the Git worktree root, use harness.py project --at PATH, where PATH is repository-relative and . selects the root. The source and test areas in openspec/workflow.yaml may be outside this directory.

Without a selector, the wrapper finds the nearest adopted OpenSpec home from the current directory. If no local home is found, it can select the sole configured project. A nearer unadopted OpenSpec home or an ambiguous choice stops selection. Review the returned home and source scope against the request. The wrapper runs the pinned CLI from that home. Preserve its returned internal id in the run's requests and evidence, even if the working directory changes.

Reuse an existing OpenSpec home through deliberate adoption. Do not initialize a second home to evade an existing project's rules, history or unfinished work. Never silently replace its config, schemas, specifications or change archive. Preserve the existing config.yaml or config.yml; two config files are ambiguous. This version requires non-overlapping registered project roots.

Use native configuration for schema selection, context, artifact rules and supported operation guidance. Use the adjacent workflow.yaml for this package's executable checks, source scope, preparation commands, lockfiles and evidence exclusions. The installer maintains the internal index; these settings have one project-owned source beside OpenSpec after migration.

OpenSpec-generated skills remain managed by OpenSpec. Keep package behavior in the sdw-* entry points and these policies. Editing generated skill bodies is not a supported customization mechanism; an OpenSpec update may replace them. Native /opsx operations do not automatically invoke this package's independent review or final acceptance. Use the sdw-* entrypoints for those procedures.

Artifacts and evidence

A proposal states the problem, scope, capabilities and dependencies. Delta specifications define observable behavior and scenarios. A design records interfaces, tradeoffs, failure behavior and verification. Tasks identify bounded implementation slices and their checks. Their existence demonstrates planning, not delivery.

Keep openspec/specs/ truthful about implemented and verified behavior. Use added requirements for new capabilities and modified or removed requirements only against an existing baseline. Do not promote proposed behavior early. Follow the pinned OpenSpec schema instead of inventing structural headings.

The built-in spec-driven schema already provides the artifacts this runtime uses. Existing custom schemas are preserved, but the runtime requires proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md and capability deltas at specs/<capability>/spec.md within each change. A schema with different outputs needs a deliberate compatibility change before this runtime can execute it. Adding a review document to a schema does not establish reviewer independence or acceptance of the final source; those checks belong to the runtime.

For maintenance without capability changes, use the supported skip_specs: true change metadata and explicit acceptance tasks. Do not fabricate a product capability merely to satisfy lifecycle checks or use this mode to avoid a real behavioral delta.

Synchronization and archive

Archive only completed and verified work. Check that synchronized requirement bodies match the approved deltas, including renames and removals. Matching headings or checked task boxes alone are insufficient.

Archive relocation changes review inputs. Retain the original evidence and bind new snapshots to affected final artifacts before acceptance. Fix relative links and references in the same change. Preserve stopped work and historical archives.

Run strict validation of the selected project after synchronization. Successful OpenSpec validation checks artifact structure; implementation tests, independent review and the final-source gate remain separate requirements.

Execute one bounded run

Read the policy map, execution policy, plan profiles and role contract. sdw-run, sdw-harden and sdw-review select the full pipeline, design phase or implementation review. Their discovery does not grant additional authority.

Commands below run from the assigned repository or worktree root. python means the interpreter prepared for the installed harness; it is not necessarily the target application's interpreter. SPEC_ROOT is the repository-relative directory containing the intended openspec/; use . for the root. JSON filenames identify the requests you prepared. Later harness.py references abbreviate python agentic_harness/tools/harness.py; use the full invocation when running them.

Resolve inputs and ownership

  1. Select the intended OpenSpec directory:

    python agentic_harness/tools/harness.py project --at SPEC_ROOT
python agentic_harness/tools/harness.py openspec --at SPEC_ROOT -- list --json

    Read the returned specification home, source scope, queue, checks and environment policy. Read native context and rules in its openspec/config.yaml (or existing config.yml) and executable settings in openspec/workflow.yaml. Keep the returned id in all machine requests for this run. The internal index preserves stable identifiers; you do not need to invent or remember one. Read the selected change and applicable target instructions. The wrapper selects that OpenSpec directory and the pinned executable.

    Omit --at when the current directory identifies the intended adopted home, or when no local home is found and only one project is configured. A nearer unadopted home or ambiguity stops selection. When tests are outside the specification home, choose their owning home explicitly. Preserve the selected binding after intake; changing directories does not change an admitted run.

  2. Record bounded intake and validate it with harness.py intake INTAKE.json. Preserve the current ticket observation outside the repository when implementation requires it. Record planning, review, implementation, publication, merge and cleanup authority separately. A remote action can be prepared locally without permission to publish it.

  3. Inspect the queue through coordination list or coordination next, supplying the repository and request. Inspection does not claim work. A separate coordination claim binds project, change, immutable base, session and generation. Coordination state lives in Git's common directory and is shared by linked worktrees on this host, not other clones or machines.

  4. Create or adopt an owned worktree with the coordination commands. Bind branch, base, allowed parent and environment ownership. Run the registered preparation commands and retain their original result. Fingerprint declared lockfiles; use explicit environment rebind after intentional lock changes. Missing dependency preparation or a dirty owned workspace requires reconciliation.

Admit and dispatch assignments

  1. Choose the run ID and retain its initial source through harness.py source capture SOURCE.json. Use a fresh destination outside the worktree and explicit nonignored source paths. Capture intended untracked files as well as committed and modified files; retain executable modes and declared deleted originals from the pinned base. Honor project exclusions and reject unsafe or secret paths. Verify the resulting bundle before use; its input_revision is the ledger's initial source revision.

  2. Initialize an external ledger using harness.py plans --db RUN.sqlite init --request RUN.json. Pin that verified input revision, plan, project, change, applicable stages, implementation slices, scope authority, context capacity and spend envelope. Preserve this ledger on resume. Inspect plans routes and run plans preflight with actual client/account evidence before launching workers. CLI help alone does not demonstrate account access or effective context capacity.

  3. Prepare a dispatch request binding intake, ledger, run ID, worktree, bundle, fresh evidence directory, assignment kind, admission, original prompt files, checks and coordination ownership. Capture each assignment's current source and reconcile changed inputs before admission; the request's input revision must match its verified bundle. Writers receive exact exclusive paths. Freeze the workspace before read-only assignments or a paired review round. Dispatch through harness.py dispatch --request ASSIGNMENT.json; it reserves capacity and records attempts before native launch.

  4. Retain original requests, prompts, native stdout/stderr, structured results and available usage. Read-only reviewers use retained source. Reproductions requiring commands are separate permitted scratch checks, retained with their results. Do not equate transport completion with successful review.

Reconcile, accept and hand off

  1. After edits, reconcile the ledger against verified source manifests and the relevant design and implementation revisions. Preserve unaffected original evidence; reset affected clean rounds when inputs change. Handle findings through the relevant design or implementation review procedure. Record any needed resource extension before exceeding a limit.

  2. Run required checks against the final source and complete the OpenSpec lifecycle. Final coverage includes changed, new and deleted paths, synchronized capability bodies, archived change artifacts, queue, native configuration, internal index and the selected openspec/workflow.yaml containing check authority. Archive relocation needs a newly bound design snapshot and affected independent acceptance. Confirm full review originals and final-source correspondence before claiming readiness.

  3. Use harness.py remote prepare, grant, execute and reconcile for the supported GitHub operations, with their JSON requests. Retain operation identity and receipts. A lost response remains unknown until reconciled against GitHub; do not blindly repeat the mutation. Publication and merge require their own applicable authority. Merge also checks the current head.

  4. Return the bounded outcome, evidence, remaining limitations and next action. Handoff never starts another queued task. Cleanup first inventories dirty files, active assignments, environment dependencies and evidence pins. Apply only an authorized inventory after rechecking protections, using normal non-forced worktree removal. Branch deletion is a separate action.

Interrupted work

Save a checkpoint containing ownership, revisions, decisions, unresolved findings, checks, originals and the next action. Reconcile all attempted writer edits before resume. Do not repeat completed commits, archival operations or external actions merely because the session restarted.

For uncertain dispatch, use harness.py dispatch --recover --request RECOVERY.json only with evidence of the original result and stopped-process outcome. Retain the uncertain receipt as history. Settle existing reservations and usage once; missing billing is not zero billing. If originals remain unavailable, report the attempt incomplete.

Request contracts

The runtime rejects unknown or missing fields. Build requests from the installed version's public contracts below, then use its CLI validation. Do not copy a historical request, fabricate an observation or guess a field to bypass a gate. JSON paths and evidence references must identify the actual assigned workspace and retained originals.

Request Defining contract
Intake and ticket observation validate_intake and ticket validation in intake.py
Initial ledger, preflight, rounds, extensions and checkpoints Ledger.init, preflight and the corresponding public Ledger method in plan_runtime.py
Project, claim, workspace, environment and cleanup CLI action mapping and corresponding public function in coordination.py
Source capture and verification materialize and verify in evidence.py
Assignment and interrupted launch execute and recover in dispatch.py
Remote operations and final acceptance Journal methods and acceptance_gate in lifecycle.py

The CLI entrypoint shows how each JSON request reaches its contract. These explicit tools require an agent or operator to assemble the bounded run; there is no unattended queue runner.

Harden one design

Use sdw-harden for one selected OpenSpec change. Read the policy map, OpenSpec policy and execution procedure. This phase prepares and independently reviews a contract; it does not authorize implementation.

  1. A combined context assignment reads the relevant current and prerequisite contracts, source interfaces and downstream expectations. It returns a bounded brief and scenario-to-test map. Report missing evidence or uncovered scope; do not survey every unrelated change or archive.

  2. One author writes or reconciles the proposal, delta specifications, design and tasks within assigned artifact paths. Specify concrete behavior, interfaces, failures, migration and tests where applicable. Preserve valid existing decisions and run strict OpenSpec validation. Retain the resulting source for independent review.

  3. Dispatch a paired design round against the same frozen inputs. The contract lens checks every scenario, acceptance criterion, interface and verification plan. The feasibility/risk lens checks determinism, recovery, concurrency, resource bounds, security and affected consumers where relevant. Reviewers use fresh identities and return complete coverage and concrete findings.

  4. Group exact duplicates deterministically while preserving original findings and IDs. For a nonempty batch, one independent adjudicator verifies each ID against cited evidence. A rejected major or blocker finding remains a dispute until evidence and independent acceptance resolve it. A vote or absence of reproduction does not waive a real defect.

  5. One assigned author/fixer resolves the confirmed batch and checks coherence in the same interval. Record each assigned finding as resolved or unresolved, validate the artifacts and retain the new inputs. Obtain fresh independent review under the selected plan; earlier reviews of changed content do not satisfy acceptance.

Use the plan's shared D counter, clean-round minimum and repair allowances. Do not impose historical source-workflow call caps. Before a repair, retain enough later review capacity or obtain the required bounded extension.

Incomplete reports, missing originals, uncovered scope, unresolved serious disputes or exhausted allowances leave this phase incomplete. Acceptance needs full coverage, required checks and the selected clean minimum on unchanged accepted inputs. Retain the complete originals outside the worktree.

Review one implementation

Use sdw-review for one selected implementation. Read the policy map and execution procedure. Review-only authority does not permit code fixes or new implementation.

Paired independent review

Supply the immutable base, full changed-path inventory, relevant specification and design sections, project checks, downstream boundaries and retained source. Both reviewers use the same frozen inputs with distinct fresh identities.

  • The behavior/test lens checks every affected capability and scenario, observable results, failure cases and test strength. For maintenance without capability deltas, it checks proposal acceptance and relevant tooling tests.
  • The runtime/safety lens checks recovery, determinism, concurrency, idempotency, resource use, security, compatibility and affected consumers where relevant.

Reviewers remain read-only. Focused reproductions requiring commands run only in separately assigned scratch space. Claim reproduction only when performed. Return the required structured result with input revision, coverage disposition, findings and a truthful truncation flag. Each finding identifies its location, violated contract, concrete impact, severity, evidence and suggested correction. Missing coverage or overflow makes the result incomplete, never clean.

Findings and repairs

Group exact duplicates deterministically and retain every original. One independent adjudicator reviews the complete nonempty batch, returning a verdict and evidence for each finding ID. Do not launch an agent per finding. A serious dispute remains blocking until evidence and a fresh independent round resolve it.

Within implementation authority, assign confirmed fixes to exact owned files. Repair code, tests and affected design coherently before the next review. Preserve authoritative requirements; a missing test is not a reason to weaken the contract. Under review-only authority, return findings for an authorized writer instead of modifying the checkout.

Acceptance

Use the selected plan's shared I counter and clean minimum. Reserve subsequent review capacity before fixes. Run relevant checks and capture the resulting source. Final integration edits invalidate affected acceptance and require new review; changing sessions cannot reset allowances.

Require complete original reports, full affected coverage, resolved defects, required passing checks and clean review on the final relevant bytes. Retain historical inputs separately. A narrow or partial review cannot be relabeled as whole-change acceptance, and the end of a budget does not establish readiness.

Execution policy

The extracted runtime uses plans-v1. Its plan catalog defines supported profiles, requested routes, context targets and attempt allowances. Follow the execution procedure; package installation does not launch workers or change a host's default model.

Bounded work and independence

A run handles one selected change and only the applicable authorized stages. Bind project, base revision, owned worktree, scope, authority, plan and evidence before dispatch. Writers receive exclusive exact paths. Read-only assignments use a retained source tree; command-based reproductions use separately assigned scratch material.

The shipped catalog permits two concurrent workers per run and no nested delegation. Coordinate slots across stages and providers. A shared ledger also accounts for other runs using that ledger. Separate ledgers do not create a host-wide quota. These are execution-profile limits, not a provider capacity claim. Host-local coordination does not coordinate separate clones or machines.

Each design or implementation review round contains two independent lenses on the same frozen inputs. Use fresh reviewer identities and contexts, distinct from authors and other independent assignments. A reviewer may resume only its same unfinished assignment against unchanged recorded inputs. Never accept an author's self-review as independent acceptance.

Apply the selected plan's clean-round and per-step rules. Failed launches and retries consume allowance; changing provider, restarting or selecting another plan does not reset counters. Reserve enough later review capacity before a repair. Missing capacity, incomplete coverage or unresolved serious findings leave the phase incomplete.

Settings and resources

Verify required model and effort availability, client options, conflicting overrides and effective context capacity before launch. Record requested and runtime-reported settings separately. Unknown settings or usage stay unknown. Do not silently substitute a model, reduce effort or use a paid tier outside the existing authority.

Context targets and concise result targets are working policies, not advertised provider windows. Partition scope while preserving coverage when inputs do not fit. Never truncate findings to obtain a clean result. Preserve complete original reports separately from concise handoffs.

When a limit must increase, request one bounded extension that covers the remaining repair, adjudication, review and verification. State used allowances, the actual blocker and evidence, added allowances and resulting ceilings, requested routes, estimates or unknown costs, and the stopping condition. Reuse an approved extension within its scope; silence is not an extension.

Evidence and recovery

Retain exact requests, prompts, complete original results, identities, timestamps, source bundles, executable modes, deleted originals and available usage records outside the worktree. Keep summaries separate. Bind check results and both review phases to the relevant final source revisions.

Missing, partial, stale, unbound or malformed reports do not count as clean. Successful transport completion is not acceptance. Wait for launched siblings to settle before dependent edits. An uncertain launch keeps its reservation until recovery establishes its outcome; never blindly replay it.

Reconcile attempted writer edits and current source before retry or resume. Preserve prior counters, evidence and remote operation receipts. A changed input invalidates affected clean rounds; a new capture cannot impersonate the original reviewed result. Review acceptance requires complete coverage, resolved defects and required passing checks against the final bytes.

The validators verify supplied records and bindings. They do not prove review depth, hidden context isolation, remote observation authenticity, production behavior or model quality. Report the scope of actual verification.

Runtime assignment contract

Read the policy map, plan profiles and execution procedure, then the assigned phase. The dispatcher binds role, provider settings, source revision, authority and allowance in its ledger. A skill or discovery adapter does not replace that run record or alter the host's default model.

Work only on the named assignment. Writers own exact listed files. Read-only roles use retained source and separately assigned scratch material for permitted reproductions. Return complete findings and coverage, including unresolved work. Do not edit the implementation checkout as a reviewer, dispatch nested agents, truncate findings to claim success or treat a failed call as free.

Preserve the exact prompt, original result, checks and input revision. Reconcile them before resuming an assignment. Unknown effective settings and usage stay unknown. Report a scope, route, context, authority or budget blocker to the lead; do not substitute settings or make an extra attempt outside the recorded limits.
